draft.title: Gradient and y-intercept
card: A straight line can be written as y = mx + c. In this form, m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept.
The y-intercept is the point where the line cuts the y-axis. It is the point (0, c), because x is 0 there.
Changing m tilts the line, making it steeper or flatter. Changing c shifts the whole line up or down without tilting it.
Example: y = −3x + 5 has gradient −3 and cuts the y-axis at (0, 5). It slopes down to the right.
draft.remember: In y = mx + c, m sets the tilt and c sets where the line meets the y-axis.

a.q: A line has the equation y = 4x − 7. What are its gradient and y-intercept?
opts: Gradient 4, y-intercept −7
Gradient −7, y-intercept 4
Gradient 4, y-intercept 7
Gradient −4, y-intercept 7
a.why: The number multiplying x is the gradient, 4. The number added on its own is the y-intercept, which is −7 here. Swapping the two numbers is a common mistake.
a.clue: The gradient is the number multiplying x.

b.q: The line y = 2x + 1 is changed to y = 2x + 6. What happens to the line?
opts: It shifts up 5 units and stays parallel
It becomes steeper and keeps its y-intercept
It shifts up 6 units and stays parallel
It becomes flatter and cuts the axis higher
b.why: The gradient m stays at 2, so the tilt does not change. The y-intercept goes from 1 to 6, which moves the line up by 6 − 1 = 5 units. Shifting by 6 units forgets that the line started at 1.
b.clue: Which number changed, m or c, and by how much?

b.best: It shifts up 5 units and stays parallel
